top_choice_rationale: P001 credits one writer, Mircea Cărtărescu, with clean attribution: one author and one principal language. On the common criteria his case is the most securely weighable on the slate. From public knowledge and translated reception, the Orbitor trilogy (Blinding is its first volume) and Solenoid show a voice that is hard to confuse with any other. They also show formal ambition sustained at very large scale and imaginative depth, as memory, the body and dream are built into one patterned metaphysical architecture. I do not count the unanimous opening support as merit. The citation should stay anchored in the large prose works and not claim the poetry or early fiction, which no member has assessed. The main uncertainties remain open. I cannot verify Romanian syntax, rhythm and density through translation. It is unsettled whether Solenoid and the later novels transform the project or only elaborate it, and the poetry and early work are thinly covered. These limits narrow the citation's scope but do not outweigh the case for an award. P000 would withhold a prize from a writer whose achievement is substantial on the evidence available, so it ranks second. This judgment rests on public knowledge and translated reception, not on a full reading or independent verification of sources.
